Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock fell 14% in the week to Oct. 30, and Datadog fell 13%, though neither company reported weak results.

ServiceNow's and Fortinet's reports revived fears that AI will disrupt software, and Friday's tech selloff did most of the damage.

Cloudflare's Nov. 5 report has to clear a guide of 31% revenue growth and show gross margin holding near 73%.

The stock is cheaper but still richly valued, and Datadog's Nov. 4 report lands first.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock fell 14% in the week to Oct. 30, closing Friday at $280.70, and Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ) fell 13% to $235.27. Neither company reported weak results. Both got caught in a software selloff that peaked on Friday.

Software's bad week

ServiceNow and Fortinet reported after the close on Oct. 28. The next day, Fortinet fell about 20% after cutting its full-year service revenue forecast, and ServiceNow fell 27%, its worst day on record. That revived the fear that AI is disrupting software.

Then on Friday, Oct. 30, weak results from Amazon and Intel deepened doubts about whether AI spending will pay off. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5%, Datadog lost 11.5%, and Cloudflare lost 9.5%.

Cloudflare had started the week right after a 7% jump on Oct. 23, as the PHP flaws lifted security stocks. CEO Matthew Prince said exploit attempts on Cloudflare's network climbed from thousands before the flaws were disclosed to millions after.

The one company-specific item was a disclosure, not a result. On Oct. 26, Cloudflare reported that a bug in one Workers AI model sent 155 responses containing other customers' data between Aug. 27 and Sept. 9. The company says it fixed the issue on Sept. 9 and found no evidence of deliberate exploitation.

Datadog is in the same boat

Datadog also had no news of its own. Its second-quarter revenue grew 36% to $1.12 billion, but its third-quarter guide of $1.135 billion to $1.145 billion implies roughly 29% growth from a year earlier. It reports before the open on Nov. 4, a day ahead of Cloudflare, so a clean beat there would ease some of the pressure on its neighbor.

The bar for Nov. 5

For the third quarter, Cloudflare guided to $736 million to $737 million of revenue (31% growth) and $0.34 of adjusted EPS. Analysts expect revenue to more than double from 2025 to 2028:

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

Nothing in the selloff gives them a reason to cut those numbers.

Gross margin is the weak spot. Cloudflare's GAAP gross margin fell to 74.5% in fiscal 2025 from 77.3% a year earlier, a decline management has tied to carrying more traffic:

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after underwhelming earnings reports from tech giants Amazon and Intel (after mediocre earnings reports from Alphabet and ServiceNow the previous day) sparked widespread investor anxiety regarding aggressive artificial intelligence spending and sustained cash burn.

As reported by CNBC, disappointing quarterly reports from both companies triggered a broad slide across technology equities and hardware suppliers, overshadowing positive momentum in other areas of the market. Investors grew increasingly wary of the sector's rising capital expenditures—the funds poured into long-term assets such as data centers and computing hardware.

With both firms spending heavily to build out artificial intelligence infrastructure, market participants are questioning when these massive investments will translate into meaningful revenue and profit growth per CNBC. The steep drops in Amazon and Intel weighed heavily on market indices, showing how vulnerabilities among dominant technology leaders can rapidly dampen confidence across the broader industry.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare shares fell 2.7% to $310 on Thursday ahead of its November 5 report, after gaining about 46% over six months.

The company guided third-quarter revenue to $736 million to $737 million, up 31%, with adjusted EPS of $0.34.

At 34x forward sales and 210x forward earnings, the stock leaves little room for a miss, and adjusted gross margin fell to 73.1% last quarter.

Watch whether net retention holds near 120% and whether management raises full-year revenue guidance of $2.864 billion to $2.870 billion.

Last week, a cluster of PHP flaws knocked government websites offline and set off a global patching scramble. Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) saw millions of exploit attempts after the disclosure.

Events like this are why customers pay Cloudflare. The stock still slipped 2.7% to $310 on Thursday.

Shares are up about 46% over the past six months but sit 16% below their 52-week high of $370. The real test comes November 5, when Cloudflare reports third-quarter results.

The bar for November 5

Cloudflare raised the bar itself in August. Second-quarter revenue rose 36% to $696.1 million, topping consensus by about $30 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.29 beat by two cents.

For the third quarter, management guided to:

Revenue of $736 million to $737 million, up 31%

Adjusted operating income of $129 million to $130 million

Adjusted EPS of $0.34

It also raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.864 billion to $2.870 billion. Management has said it guides carefully because more deals now run on consumption and pool-of-funds contracts, which are harder to forecast.

Here's the trend heading into the print…

Cloudflare (NET): total revenue, quarterly, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, Q1 2025–Q4 2026 (TIKR)

Growth would cool to 31% if Cloudflare lands on its guide. A beat like the second quarter's would keep it in the mid 30s.

Machines are becoming the customer

CEO Matthew Prince framed the opportunity boldly in the second-quarter release. AI answer engines and agent-driven commerce are driving "a fundamental rewrite of the Internet for machine-to-machine traffic," he said.

The customer data backs him up. Cloudflare's developer base topped 10 million, up from 7.4 million a quarter earlier. Large customers rose 27% to 4,698 and now drive 73% of revenue.

Existing customers are spending more too. Dollar-based net retention climbed to 120%, up six points from a year ago, and current remaining performance obligations grew 35%.

Now compare that with the older incumbent…

Cloudflare (NET): total revenue vs Akamai (AKAM), $ billions, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

Akamai (AKAM:NASDAQ) grew second-quarter revenue just 5% to $1.1 billion. Its cloud infrastructure unit grew 39%, but on only $99 million of revenue, so Cloudflare is closing the size gap fast.

title: Why Did Cloudflare Stock Jump?
detail:
Why Did Cloudflare Stock Jump?
Trefis Team

Shares of Cloudflare (NET) climbed 79.7% from January 31 to October 28, 2026, outpacing the 12.5% return of the S&P 500. The advance spanned three quarterly reports, ending with the most recent on August 6. The path was uneven: shares fell 23.6% on May 8, after the first-quarter report came with a 20% staff cut, and rose 10.5% on September 9 on a security partnership with OpenAI. The current share price appears to assume that developers and AI companies will sustain fast enough sales growth for the company to reach a reported profit. So are Cloudflare's sales really growing faster?

Cloudflare's Sales Are Growing Faster Than A Year Ago

So far, yes. Cloudflare generated $696 million in sales during the second quarter of fiscal 2026, reported on August 6. Revenue grew 35.9% in the quarter, compared with a 27.8% pace in the same period a year earlier.

The company is also securing larger contracts. Cloudflare announced in its February 10 report that it closed its largest deal on record by annual contract value, averaging $42.5 million a year. By the August 6 call, the number of customers paying more than $100,000 a year climbed 27% from a year earlier.

Management credits rapid growth in its Workers developer platform in particular. The company's own outlook is slower, however. Cloudflare guided to third-quarter revenue growth of 31%, with management stating they set guidance prudently as a shift toward pool-of-funds and consumption-based deals makes each quarter harder to forecast.

How Far Has Cloudflare's Operating Loss Narrowed?

Over the twelve months ending in June 2026, Cloudflare posted an operating loss equal to 8.1% of revenue. That margin narrowed from 9.9% a year earlier and 11.6% two years earlier.

The company's net loss widened to $170 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, up from $50.4 million a year earlier. Management reported $151 million in severance and other restructuring charges for the quarter. The filings data records those charges below the operating line, so the 8.1% operating loss above leaves them out. Without those expenses, executives said the net loss would have been roughly $18 million.

During the August 6 call, management said Cloudflare is pacing ahead of its goal to reach a GAAP profit by the end of 2028 at the latest. That is a target, not a result.

What Are You Paying For Cloudflare's Sales Now?

At the October 28 close, investors paid 45.0 times Cloudflare's sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.2 times for the S&P 500. Based on those same twelve months of sales, the multiple was 34.6 at the end of June. The valuation climb since then has come from a higher price on revenue Cloudflare had already reported.

Cloudflare (NET) stock rose 7.3% on Friday, October 23, 2026, while the S&P 500 fell 0.5%. The company released no earnings report around the move, yet every company on its peer list advanced during the session. So what lifted Cloudflare and those companies on a day the market fell?

What Happened To Cloud Software Stocks On Friday?

News reports on October 23 noted a broadening rebound in cloud software stocks, with edge delivery companies setting the pace. A technology stock selloff also showed signs of easing at the close of what reports called a rollercoaster week. The wider market moved in the opposite direction, with U.S. stocks declining as oil prices climbed to their highest level in five months, news reports said.

For context, in its latest results for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, management said growth was driven in particular by its Workers developer platform, which developers use to build their software, and by agentic workloads across its network. The company posted revenue of $696 million for the quarter, an increase of 35.9% from a year earlier.

Did Cloudflare Rise On Its Own That Day?

No. The broader advance is visible among the companies on its Trefis peer list. Zscaler gained 7.3%, matching Cloudflare, while Fastly rose 8.7%. Akamai Technologies, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet also traded higher during the session.

The technology sector as a whole posted much smaller gains, with the SPDR fund tracking the sector, XLK, rising 0.5%. Cloudflare's rise was part of a move across its peer group rather than an isolated advance.

Where Cloudflare Stock Stands After The Rise

Moves of this magnitude are not rare for Cloudflare. The stock recorded 12 sessions with a rise at least this large over the previous year, most recently posting an 8.7% gain on September 21, 2026.

Cloudflare stock returned 54.6% over the past 12 months, compared to 15.1% for the S&P 500. Performance over the past month moved the other way, with the shares falling 9.2% from September 24 to October 23 while the S&P 500 fell 1.0%. Friday's close of $325.73 kept the stock below its 52-week closing high of $360.93, set on October 9. The stock reached its 52-week closing low of $160.19 on February 23.

If you buy the stock now, you will pay 45.9 times Cloudflare's sales over the past twelve months, compared to 3.2 times for the S&P 500.

Cloudflare's next financial report will cover the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Revenue is the measure to watch in that release, with management guiding to a range of $736 million to $737 million on its August 6 call.
